question.text: A Cat III AIF holds 1,000 corporate bonds with face value Rs. 1,00,000 each, coupon 9%, purchased at a clean price of 105 (i.e., 105% of face value, or Rs. 1,05,000 per bond). What is the gross holding value at purchase?

explanation.text: The Logic: Price per bond = 105% x face value = 1.05 x Rs. 1,00,000 = Rs. 1,05,000. Total holding value = 1,000 bonds x Rs. 1,05,000 = Rs. 10,50,00,000 = Rs. 10.50 crore. This matches the workbook's tabulated amount of Rs. 10,50,00,000 (pp. 270-271). The Trap: Option A (Rs. 1 crore) and option D (Rs. 10 crore) ignore the premium and the correct number of bonds respectively. Option C (Rs. 1.05 crore) is what you would obtain if you (incorrectly) assumed Rs. 10,000 face value with a Rs. 10,500 per-bond price (1,000 x Rs. 10,500 = Rs. 1.05 crore) - this is the arithmetic that would have been correct had the face value been Rs. 10,000. Note: The original stem stated face value Rs. 10,000, which under standard bond-price arithmetic gives Rs. 10,500 per bond and Rs. 1.05 crore total - inconsistent with the workbook's tabulated Rs. 10,50,00,000. The face value in the stem has been corrected to Rs. 1,00,000 so the standard arithmetic reconciles with the workbook amount and the keyed answer is uniquely supported. Source: Series-XIX-B AIF (Category III) Distributors-December workbook, pp. 270-271.
